relevanceRationale.transferable: Identity, empty guards and preserved order transfer to other list tasks.

relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Opaque and NaN values catch corruption hidden by primitive examples.

defects: Senior used splice instead of the requested shift.
Exact returned-array ownership, bounds and opaque values were unspecified.
Returning a copied array or replacing a NaN item passed old checks.
rationale: Align senior with shift/push and state a bounded ordinary mutable dense-array domain. Preserve exact values and caller-list identity even for empty/singleton inputs. Add frozen element identities, NaN/undefined/signed zero and a 10000-item rotation. Explain linear front removal under the usual array movement model. Manual supplied-source reading establishes method conformance; finite cases do not prove arbitrary learner source style.

Cases reject rounding and source sorting; this is a Number exercise rather than exact monetary arithmetic.

objective: Build a fresh integer countdown with while/push and an explicit output-size cost model.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: while loops and bounded output generation remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Expressing a positive stopping condition is a useful basic exercise.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Termination, fresh results and output-sensitive cost transfer elsewhere.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The foundation task should show while rather than a direct array constructor.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Large outputs and repeated empty calls catch hidden caps and shared arrays.

defects: Senior used Array.from rather than the required while loop.
The hint falsely said the number of values could not be known in advance.
Integer bounds and fresh empty-result ownership were unspecified.
rationale: Use while/push on every board, with bounded integer start and positive integer step so subtraction terminates safely. Replace the false unknown-length claim with a direct stopping-condition explanation. Define n as1+the nonnegative ceiling quotient, reflecting output length, not raw start alone. Add10000 generated values, a near-start-size step, negative/zero starts and distinct empty/nonempty arrays across calls. Cases reject an arbitrary output cap and a shared empty singleton.
